shared_elements: large upright stone monument on a museum plinth
single dominant anthropomorphic figure filling the field
elaborate headdress/headgear occupying the upper zone
circular disc or medallion motif (chest/ear ornament)
banded belt-like horizontal element across the torso
justification: Both are monumental stones dominated by a single costumed human figure whose broad headdress fills the upper zone above a torso bearing a disc ornament and a banded belt, and both are carved in shallow linear relief. The decisive difference is medium and manner: A is a rounded, deeply weathered three-dimensional dark volcanic boulder-sculpture with eroded frontal features, while B is a flat pale slab carved in crisp, controlled low relief with a profile figure and an adjacent panel of rectangular glyph-like blocks.
